Secured

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
A paramilitary security company accused of using strongarm tactics to restrict access to the forest.
A paramilitary security company accused of assault and murder in a small farming town.

Summary:
As South Africa's police force dwindles in numbers and capacity, the private security industry is booming. Farming commuities, privaate compnies anfd even the SAPS are using private security firms to secure them. Its against this backdrop that Magma Security was hire in Hogsback and Dodrecht to protects local assets but their methods are being called into question.

Further information:
Hogsback, a picturesque village in the Eastern Cape renowned for its hiking trails and biodiversity, is facing a significant decline in tourism. This downturn follows the actions of a local forestry company that has enclosed traditional walking routes with non-indigenous pine plantations and stationed armed guards at nearly all access points. These trails, cherished by both locals and visitors for over 80 years, are now largely inaccessible, leading to a downturn in the local economy, which heavily relies on tourism during holiday seasons.

The presence of paramilitary-style security personnel has raised concerns among residents and tourists alike. While private security firms play a role in supplementing public safety, there are stringent regulations governing their operations. According to the Private Security Industry Regulation Act of 2001, security guards are restricted fromengaging in activities such as crowd control unless specifically accredited. Additionally, their powers do not extend to automatic stop-and-search procedures without proper authorization.

Two hours away in the small town of Dordrecht, the farming community has secured the services of Magma Security as well. There, the allegations turn darker - extending to murder.

Murdered Case Study Family

Deceased - Mziyanda Msebenzi
Age - 34 years
Occupation - Unemployed
Date of incident - 3 March 2025
Location - Dordrecht, Zola Location
Cas no - 07/03/2025
Details of incident - Mziyanda Msebenzi was last seen on Monday being dragged by a security company in Dordrecht called MAGMA. The cousin says a white gentleman called MAGMA to assist him in chasing down a group he accused of robbing him. It was Mziyanda and two of his friends that were being chased. Mziyanda’s friends claim that one of the MAGMA security officers stomped Mziyanda with his hard security boots on the chest,he was unable to breathe and became unconscious. According to the two witness accounts, MAGMA immediately poured water on Mziyanda in an effort to revive him. MAGMA then instructed the two friends (witnesses) to leave. That was the last time Mziyanda Msebenzi was seen alive. The family searched for Mziyanda and reported him as a missing person. Mziyanda’s body was later found decomposed in Zwitwater Village. The family is resolute that MAGMA security must account for the murder and disposal of Mziyanda on a random rubbish heap.

Supporting Complainants
Lele Fred - Left arm is paralysed after being shot by Magma security. Lele says in 2023, he was sitting in a tavern when MAGMA came in guns ablazing to settle a dispute between a couple. For some unknown reason, MAGMA fired indiscriminately and as a result he was shot in the arm.

Sibongile Gentsu - accuses MAGMA of beating him up without just cause leaving his face scarred..

Magma Security Script

(Erin) I'm vertically challenged.

(Shane Eades) response is incoherent.

(Erin) The Amathole region is the central part of the Eastern Cape province, stretching along the sunshine coast. It’s an area famous for its indigenous forests.

(Erin) Many people here owe their living to what nature offers, building businesses in tourism and hospitality. 

(Shane Eades)This is my back gate onto forestry over here...

(Erin) Shane Eades runs a backpackers and 38-acre eco farm close to the small town of Hogsback. He also offers horse rides in the surrounding forests.

(Shane Eades) It's a small business. We have backpackers or eco lodge that sleeps about 20 to 25 people.

(Erin) I’m deep in the Amathole Mountains of the Eastern Cape and it’s brimming with life. Some say if you’re lucky you may get to see the fairies. 
But locals say even taking a walk in peace has become a fantasy.

(Erin) For almost a century people could wander freely through these forests, but not anymore.

(Shane Eades) They've told me no, I can't have my dog with me when I'm horse riding. I need a permit. Ladies swimming in their costumes in the dam and all of a sudden these guys come with guns and are quite rude and horrible to them and it's quite violating.
(Shane Eades) They arrived here in droves with assault rifles on their backs.

(Erin) While 22 trails in Hogsback remain permit-free, access to the rest is either restricted or denied.

(Erin) It’s hard to imagine anything disrupting the peace but one security company is accused of doing just that, in a seriously violent way.

(Erin) They’re called Magma Security and Investigations. A constant presence on the trails for the past few years, they’re accused of bullyboy tactics, intimidation, harassment… and even murder.

(Shane Eades) We were all scared. So we stopped doing rides, I had to put staff off, it was December. We were all freaked out in peak season.

(Shane Eades) I've lost staff over the years. We've always had about 8 staff, but now we're down to four permanent, five maybe.

(Erin) This region is also known for its commercial plantations. A firm called the Amathole Forestry Company or AFC manages most of the roughly 15 thousand hectares of state-owned plantations.
(Mark Andersen) We’re going to high tail it down to …

(Erin) Mark Andersen has lived in Hogsback for more than 60 years.

(Mark Andersen) We've been told several times we're very privileged to drive this. We're not allowed to bring vehicles here without very special permission so please feel grateful.

(Erin) By law, state forests are open to the public for recreational, educational, cultural, or spiritual purposes. But restrictions are allowed under some circumstances. Our tour of this forest required special permission, and we were escorted by a plantation manager.
(Erin:) Hi there, I’m Erin.

(Mark Andersen) 80% of our historic trails, trails that have been used for years have been restricted or aren't recognized as trails anymore.
(Erin) In the past, the state patrolled its own forests - but security now falls to private companies. About four years ago, AFC restricted access to the majority of these forests - and employed Magma to handle security.

(Erin) It’s alleged Magma operates as a law unto itself.

(Mark Andersen) You’ve got to be pretty sure-footed in the mud.

(Erin) Mark owns the historic Hogsback Inn. Like many small businesses, he struggled through the pandemic.
(Mark Andersen) COVID hit us as subtly as a sledgehammer. But having survived COVID, I think people in South Africa wanted to really get out into the open air after all the confinement. So Hogsback boomed for a short period of time.
(Erin) The boom brought its own problems… and a local AFC official suggested a solution.
(Mark Andersen) I got a phone call from the local plantation manager saying what do I think about him bringing in a security company for a few key days when we're basically overwhelmed? And I said ahh, fantastic idea!

(Erin) But what was supposed to be a temporary increase in security became unexpected, permanent restrictions on access to most of the forest. And the sleepy little town suddenly found itself awash with security personnel brandishing automatic rifles.
(Mark Andersen) No induction, no introduction, no training. They're in a tourist village, a little peaceful, quiet, law-abiding village and suddenly you had these guys standing in the main road, automatic weapons, paramilitary gear. Very intimidating.
(Erin) AFC refutes Mark’s claim that no consultation took place and says a meeting was held to engage the community in November 2021.

(Erin) This is a story about two very different towns. But they have one alleged villain in common: Magma Security
(Erin) It’s a forgotten town, there’s no infrastructure, there's no governance.

(Erin) Dordrecht is around 200km from Hogsback, and feels like another world.
(Ernest Elefu) Dordrecht is a small town but it’s a cursed place.
(Erin) Just a few months ago, a man called Mziyanda Msebenzi was killed here. His cousin, Ernest Elefu, says Magma employees were responsible.
(Ernest Elefu) This murder, everybody is aware of it and you don’t update the family, you don't say anything.


(Ernest Elefu) As we speak now, no arrest was effected. Nothing has been done to Magma.

(Erin) The exact circumstances around the alleged murder are unclear but this man says he was with Mziyanda at the time.

(Erin) How many Magma guys were there?

(Eyewitness)(Subtitles) Maybe it's ten or eleven.

(Erin) He, Mziyanda and another man were involved in a dispute of some kind on this rugby field.

(Eyewitness)(Subtitles) They pulled out guns on us - one tripped us and many of them had guns - and they told us to get in the car.

(Erin) He says the three of them were taken to this house and beaten with sjamboks.

(Eyewitness)(Subtitles) TaMzito was on his knees where the door was.They kicked him in his chest and he fell on his back.

(Erin) He says he and the other man were chased away, but Mziyanda lay unmoving on the floor.

(Erin) Two days later, his body was found on a rubbish heap more than 200km away.


(Ernest Elefu) Magma Security is tormenting the people of Dordrecht - first they came here to deal with stock theft but they've extended themselves to be police officers. The reason why they do that is because the police officers in Dordrecht are not doing their job.

(Erin) How are they getting away with that?

(Ernest Elefu) It's because the police officers are worshipping them instead of arresting them.

(Erin) As night falls, we hear about another chilling incident.

(Erin) It’s outside this tavern that Magma Security allegedly fired indiscriminately on a busy street.

(Erin) Two years ago, Mxolelani Mondile, was caught in an altercation outside the tavern between locals and Magma personnel.

(Mxolelani Mondile) They started to shoot because I just heard (makes supposed sound of gunshot), the arm just goes down. I heard the second shot, it’s when I decided no, let me lie down.

(Erin) Mxolelani’s left arm was paralysed and as a result he lost his job. A Magma employee has been charged with attempted murder but is reportedly still patrolling the streets of Dordrecht.

(Erin) The police didn’t respond to specific allegations that they allow Magma to operate as it pleases in Dordrecht. They confirmed that both reported incidents are under investigation.

(Erin) In Hogsback, too, intimidation allegedly spilled over into violence as far back as 2021.

(Mark Andersen) The local that was assaulted by them was actually a member of the Hogsback CPF committee at the time. This is the 11th of December 2021.
(Erin) It’s alleged the Community Policing Forum Member was dragged from his car by Magma personnel and was so seriously assaulted that he needed hospital care.
(Erin) The incident was a tipping point in the town’s relations with Magma.

(Mark Andersen) Very upsetting because he's well regarded in his community. It was an injury for the whole community which resulted in them rioting.
(Erin) The community took to the streets.
(Mark Andersen) The crowd started coming down the road. Magma went into the main road of Hogsback and fired live ammunition over their heads. You know, in the air as an intimidatory tactic to stop them.

(Erin) The Amathole Forestry Company told us that historic access to some of the trails wasn’t necessarily lawful. It says Magma’s presence on the trails is purely a response to a spike in crime.
(Erin) But the locals we spoke to reject this claim, and are taking the company on in court, demanding access to the trails.
(Mark Andersen) We were told off the record by a previous employee of theirs, that if AFC had their way they would fence off the forest and not let anybody in. They certainly want to shut off a very large part of the forest.
(Erin) On your allegation or version, AFC wants to close ranks around the forests and Magma is their muscle.
(Mark Andersen) Yes, Magma is their muscle, they’re the enforcers.

(Erin) Magma agreed to an interview.

(Henrico Pretorius) We are aware of the status of Hogsback town itself and that it's a tourist destination so therefore, we brief our personnel accordingly.

(Erin) Henrico Pretorius is General Manager of Magma Security and Investigations in the Eastern Cape. We begin with the CPF member’s assault and hospitalisation four years ago – an incident Pretorius says he wasn’t even aware of.

(Henrico Pretorius) Well, the specific incident was brought to my attention by yourselves. And I can only explain due process of how we deal with it and what should have happened.

(Erin) But what did happen?

(Henrico Pretorius) I wasn't in a position to actually find out what the case number was.

(Erin) That's the police process. I'm talking about the internal process.

(Henrico Pretorius) I see no reason why internal processes would not have been followed.

(Erin) How hard is it to find that information internally? Surely it's just a quick phone call to the HR manager?

(Henrico Pretorius) Jahh no, definitely, I don't think it's difficult.

(Erin) Next, we ask about the Magma employee accused of attempting to murder Mxolelani Mondile.

(Henrico Pretorius) I'm aware of that incident. And it's currently before the court and due process will follow.

(Erin) This individual says that he has seen the same officer from Magma now on the ground, in Dordrecht, armed and working for the company.

(Henrico Pretorius) So it was decided not to suspend this member in particular.

(Erin) Do you know why?

(Henrico) And he has to, according to his bail conditions report every Friday at Dordrecht. We however, redeployed him and he’s not currently operational in Dordrecht

(Erin) But he is operational.

(Henrico Pretorius) We are of the opinion with the facts in front of us, that he's no threat and he can continue services.

(Erin) In the face of rampant crime and inadequate policing, private security companies have stepped into the breach - and it may get violent. But are Magma’s officers crossing the line?


(Erin) You're also accused of murdering a young man in a house just across the road from the church. There's an allegation from eyewitnesses… and you've rolled your eyes.

(Henrico Pretorius) I'm not rolling…. I'm taking this seriously. I regard this, what you put to me here, as very serious.

(Erin) You have a case number, what's been done internally?

(Henrico Pretorius)The South African Police services are involved and they're investigating the matter.

(Henrico Pretorius) We are not above the law, —- we work with the police — and we're not a law unto ourselves.

(Henrico Pretorius) And I think it's also in the interest of the clients, you know, if any sign or suspicion of malpractice, misconduct…

(Erin) Murder?

(Henrico Pretorius) Must be brought to our attention.

(Erin) By Magma’s own admission, the officers allegedly involved in Mziyanda’s murder also remain armed and on duty.

(Erin) We come to places like this to get away from crime in the city. There’s that sense of peace and safety - until you realise you may be at the mercy of a private security company accused of being a law unto itself.

(Erin) Shane Eades runs a backpackers and 38-acre eco farm close to the small town of Hogsback. He also offers horse rides in the surrounding forests. (Shane Eades) It's a small business. We have backpackers or eco lodge that sleeps about 20 to 25 people. (Erin) I’m deep in the Amathole Mountains of the Eastern Cape and it’s brimming with life. Some say if you’re lucky you may get to see the fairies. But locals say even taking a walk in peace has become a fantasy. (Erin) For almost a century people could wander freely through these forests, but not anymore. (Shane Eades) They've told me no, I can't have my dog with me when I'm horse riding. I need a permit. Ladies swimming in their costumes in the dam and all of a sudden these guys come with guns and are quite rude and horrible to them and it's quite violating. (Shane Eades) They arrived here in droves with assault rifles on their backs. (Erin) While 22 trails in Hogsback remain permit-free, access to the rest is either restricted or denied. (Erin) It’s hard to imagine anything disrupting the peace but one security company is accused of doing just that, in a seriously violent way. (Erin) They’re called Magma Security and Investigations. A constant presence on the trails for the past few years, they’re accused of bullyboy tactics, intimidation, harassment… and even murder. (Shane Eades) We were all scared. So we stopped doing rides, I had to put staff off, it was December. We were all freaked out in peak season. (Shane Eades) I've lost staff over the years. We've always had about 8 staff, but now we're down to four permanent, five maybe. (Erin) This region is also known for its commercial plantations. A firm called the Amathole Forestry Company or AFC manages most of the roughly 15 thousand hectares of state-owned plantations. (Mark Andersen) We’re going to high tail it down to … (Erin) Mark Andersen has lived in Hogsback for more than 60 years. (Mark Andersen) We've been told several times we're very privileged to drive this. We're not allowed to bring vehicles here without very special permission so please feel grateful. (Erin) By law, state forests are open to the public for recreational, educational, cultural, or spiritual purposes. But restrictions are allowed under some circumstances. Our tour of this forest required special permission, and we were escorted by a plantation manager. (Erin:) Hi there, I’m Erin. (Mark Andersen) 80% of our historic trails, trails that have been used for years have been restricted or aren't recognized as trails anymore. (Erin) In the past, the state patrolled its own forests - but security now falls to private companies. About four years ago, AFC restricted access to the majority of these forests - and employed Magma to handle security. (Erin) It’s alleged Magma operates as a law unto itself. (Mark Andersen) You’ve got to be pretty sure-footed in the mud. (Erin) Mark owns the historic Hogsback Inn. Like many small businesses, he struggled through the pandemic. (Mark Andersen) COVID hit us as subtly as a sledgehammer. But having survived COVID, I think people in South Africa wanted to really get out into the open air after all the confinement. So Hogsback boomed for a short period of time. (Erin) The boom brought its own problems… and a local AFC official suggested a solution. (Mark Andersen) I got a phone call from the local plantation manager saying what do I think about him bringing in a security company for a few key days when we're basically overwhelmed? And I said ahh, fantastic idea! (Erin) But what was supposed to be a temporary increase in security became unexpected, permanent restrictions on access to most of the forest. And the sleepy little town suddenly found itself awash with security personnel brandishing automatic rifles. (Mark Andersen) No induction, no introduction, no training. They're in a tourist village, a little peaceful, quiet, law-abiding village and suddenly you had these guys standing in the main road, automatic weapons, paramilitary gear. Very intimidating. (Erin) AFC refutes Mark’s claim that no consultation took place and says a meeting was held to engage the community in November 2021. (Erin) This is a story about two very different towns. But they have one alleged villain in common: Magma Security (Erin) It’s a forgotten town, there’s no infrastructure, there's no governance. (Erin) Dordrecht is around 200km from Hogsback, and feels like another world. (Ernest Elefu) Dordrecht is a small town but it’s a cursed place. (Erin) Just a few months ago, a man called Mziyanda Msebenzi was killed here. His cousin, Ernest Elefu, says Magma employees were responsible. (Ernest Elefu) This murder, everybody is aware of it and you don’t update the family, you don't say anything. (Ernest Elefu) As we speak now, no arrest was effected. Nothing has been done to Magma. (Erin) The exact circumstances around the alleged murder are unclear but this man says he was with Mziyanda at the time. (Erin) How many Magma guys were there? (Eyewitness)(Subtitles) Maybe it's ten or eleven. (Erin) He, Mziyanda and another man were involved in a dispute of some kind on this rugby field. (Eyewitness)(Subtitles) They pulled out guns on us - one tripped us and many of them had guns - and they told us to get in the car. (Erin) He says the three of them were taken to this house and beaten with sjamboks. (Eyewitness)(Subtitles) TaMzito was on his knees where the door was.They kicked him in his chest and he fell on his back. (Erin) He says he and the other man were chased away, but Mziyanda lay unmoving on the floor. (Erin) Two days later, his body was found on a rubbish heap more than 200km away. (Ernest Elefu) Magma Security is tormenting the people of Dordrecht - first they came here to deal with stock theft but they've extended themselves to be police officers. The reason why they do that is because the police officers in Dordrecht are not doing their job. (Erin) How are they getting away with that? (Ernest Elefu) It's because the police officers are worshipping them instead of arresting them. (Erin) As night falls, we hear about another chilling incident. (Erin) It’s outside this tavern that Magma Security allegedly fired indiscriminately on a busy street. (Erin) Two years ago, Mxolelani Mondile, was caught in an altercation outside the tavern between locals and Magma personnel. (Mxolelani Mondile) They started to shoot because I just heard (makes supposed sound of gunshot), the arm just goes down. I heard the second shot, it’s when I decided no, let me lie down. (Erin) Mxolelani’s left arm was paralysed and as a result he lost his job. A Magma employee has been charged with attempted murder but is reportedly still patrolling the streets of Dordrecht. (Erin) The police didn’t respond to specific allegations that they allow Magma to operate as it pleases in Dordrecht. They confirmed that both reported incidents are under investigation. (Erin) In Hogsback, too, intimidation allegedly spilled over into violence as far back as 2021. (Mark Andersen) The local that was assaulted by them was actually a member of the Hogsback CPF committee at the time. This is the 11th of December 2021. (Erin) It’s alleged the Community Policing Forum Member was dragged from his car by Magma personnel and was so seriously assaulted that he needed hospital care. (Erin) The incident was a tipping point in the town’s relations with Magma. (Mark Andersen) Very upsetting because he's well regarded in his community. It was an injury for the whole community which resulted in them rioting. (Erin) The community took to the streets. (Mark Andersen) The crowd started coming down the road. Magma went into the main road of Hogsback and fired live ammunition over their heads. You know, in the air as an intimidatory tactic to stop them. (Erin) The Amathole Forestry Company told us that historic access to some of the trails wasn’t necessarily lawful. It says Magma’s presence on the trails is purely a response to a spike in crime. (Erin) But the locals we spoke to reject this claim, and are taking the company on in court, demanding access to the trails. (Mark Andersen) We were told off the record by a previous employee of theirs, that if AFC had their way they would fence off the forest and not let anybody in. They certainly want to shut off a very large part of the forest. (Erin) On your allegation or version, AFC wants to close ranks around the forests and Magma is their muscle. (Mark Andersen) Yes, Magma is their muscle, they’re the enforcers. (Erin) Magma agreed to an interview. (Henrico Pretorius) We are aware of the status of Hogsback town itself and that it's a tourist destination so therefore, we brief our personnel accordingly. (Erin) Henrico Pretorius is General Manager of Magma Security and Investigations in the Eastern Cape. We begin with the CPF member’s assault and hospitalisation four years ago – an incident Pretorius says he wasn’t even aware of. (Henrico Pretorius) Well, the specific incident was brought to my attention by yourselves. And I can only explain due process of how we deal with it and what should have happened. (Erin) But what did happen? (Henrico Pretorius) I wasn't in a position to actually find out what the case number was. (Erin) That's the police process. I'm talking about the internal process. (Henrico Pretorius) I see no reason why internal processes would not have been followed. (Erin) How hard is it to find that information internally? Surely it's just a quick phone call to the HR manager? (Henrico Pretorius) Jahh no, definitely, I don't think it's difficult. (Erin) Next, we ask about the Magma employee accused of attempting to murder Mxolelani Mondile. (Henrico Pretorius) I'm aware of that incident. And it's currently before the court and due process will follow. (Erin) This individual says that he has seen the same officer from Magma now on the ground, in Dordrecht, armed and working for the company. (Henrico Pretorius) So it was decided not to suspend this member in particular. (Erin) Do you know why? (Henrico) And he has to, according to his bail conditions report every Friday at Dordrecht. We however, redeployed him and he’s not currently operational in Dordrecht (Erin) But he is operational. (Henrico Pretorius) We are of the opinion with the facts in front of us, that he's no threat and he can continue services. (Erin) In the face of rampant crime and inadequate policing, private security companies have stepped into the breach - and it may get violent. But are Magma’s officers crossing the line? (Erin) You're also accused of murdering a young man in a house just across the road from the church. There's an allegation from eyewitnesses… and you've rolled your eyes. (Henrico Pretorius) I'm not rolling…. I'm taking this seriously. I regard this, what you put to me here, as very serious. (Erin) You have a case number, what's been done internally? (Henrico Pretorius)The South African Police services are involved and they're investigating the matter. (Henrico Pretorius) We are not above the law, —- we work with the police — and we're not a law unto ourselves. (Henrico Pretorius) And I think it's also in the interest of the clients, you know, if any sign or suspicion of malpractice, misconduct… (Erin) Murder? (Henrico Pretorius) Must be brought to our attention. (Erin) By Magma’s own admission, the officers allegedly involved in Mziyanda’s murder also remain armed and on duty. (Erin) We come to places like this to get away from crime in the city. There’s that sense of peace and safety - until you realise you may be at the mercy of a private security company accused of being a law unto itself.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: A paramilitary security company accused of using strongarm tactics to restrict access to the forest. A paramilitary security company accused of assault and murder in a small farming town.
metadata.Summary: As South Africa's police force dwindles in numbers and capacity, the private security industry is booming. Farming commuities, privaate compnies anfd even the SAPS are using private security firms to secure them. Its against this backdrop that Magma Security was hire in Hogsback and Dodrecht to protects local assets but their methods are being called into question.
metadata.Further information: Hogsback, a picturesque village in the Eastern Cape renowned for its hiking trails and biodiversity, is facing a significant decline in tourism. This downturn follows the actions of a local forestry company that has enclosed traditional walking routes with non-indigenous pine plantations and stationed armed guards at nearly all access points. These trails, cherished by both locals and visitors for over 80 years, are now largely inaccessible, leading to a downturn in the local economy, which heavily relies on tourism during holiday seasons. The presence of paramilitary-style security personnel has raised concerns among residents and tourists alike. While private security firms play a role in supplementing public safety, there are stringent regulations governing their operations. According to the Private Security Industry Regulation Act of 2001, security guards are restricted fromengaging in activities such as crowd control unless specifically accredited. Additionally, their powers do not extend to automatic stop-and-search procedures without proper authorization. Two hours away in the small town of Dordrecht, the farming community has secured the services of Magma Security as well. There, the allegations turn darker - extending to murder. Murdered Case Study Family Deceased - Mziyanda Msebenzi Age - 34 years Occupation - Unemployed Date of incident - 3 March 2025 Location - Dordrecht, Zola Location Cas no - 07/03/2025 Details of incident - Mziyanda Msebenzi was last seen on Monday being dragged by a security company in Dordrecht called MAGMA. The cousin says a white gentleman called MAGMA to assist him in chasing down a group he accused of robbing him. It was Mziyanda and two of his friends that were being chased. Mziyanda’s friends claim that one of the MAGMA security officers stomped Mziyanda with his hard security boots on the chest,he was unable to breathe and became unconscious. According to the two witness accounts, MAGMA immediately poured water on Mziyanda in an effort to revive him. MAGMA then instructed the two friends (witnesses) to leave. That was the last time Mziyanda Msebenzi was seen alive. The family searched for Mziyanda and reported him as a missing person. Mziyanda’s body was later found decomposed in Zwitwater Village. The family is resolute that MAGMA security must account for the murder and disposal of Mziyanda on a random rubbish heap. Supporting Complainants Lele Fred - Left arm is paralysed after being shot by Magma security. Lele says in 2023, he was sitting in a tavern when MAGMA came in guns ablazing to settle a dispute between a couple. For some unknown reason, MAGMA fired indiscriminately and as a result he was shot in the arm. Sibongile Gentsu - accuses MAGMA of beating him up without just cause leaving his face scarred..
